items.title: Warren Bernhardt interviewed by Monk Rowe, Bearsville, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: Gene Lees, who was the editor at Down Beat and he was a good friend and he was a songwriter and a singer and I’d accompanied him in Chicago and in the Midwest.

ctx.x: Yeah. I mean did you find in the early sixties, in New York City, did you have to do non- musical jobs to help pay the rent?

Well Columbia brought us here and my first gig was at the Village Vanguard for a week. But actually that was after we’d been here a couple of weeks. My first day in New York, in ’62, it was in September I think, Gene Lees, who was the editor at Down Beat and he was a good friend and he was a songwriter and a singer and I’d accompanied him in Chicago and in the Midwest. He called up and he said, “Hey I’m having breakfast with Bill Evans, you want to come?” It was my first day in New York. So we go to the Olympia…
